overview: Cancer is a leading cause of death for children and adolescents. The likelihood of surviving a diagnosis of childhood cancer depends on the country in which the child lives; in high-income countries, more than 80% of children with cancer are cured, but in many LMICs less than 30% are cured.
diagnosis: determining the extent to which a cancer has spread
prevention: vaccination against hepatitis B to help prevent liver cancer
vaccination against human papillomavirus to help prevent cervical cancer
early detection and treatment of chronic infections that can lead to cancer
key_facts: An estimated 400,000 children and adolescents of 0–19 years old develop cancer each year.
More than 80% of children with cancer are cured in high-income countries, but less than 30% are cured in many LMICs.
Approximately 10% of all children with cancer have a predisposition because of genetic factors.
